ops.title: C4 disposition: subject key stays (session, scope) — PID must never join it
ops.body:
Assessed adding ClaudePID to the interaction subject key (cc-interact enforces UNIQUE(session_id, scope); envelopes carry (session, scope, pid)). Verdict: PID-in-key is wrong. cc-interact's `subject.Resolver.Start` resolves by exact (session, scope) first and CAS-rebinds `claude_pid` toward the envelope's window (`store.Rebind`: `UPDATE ... WHERE id=? AND claude_pid=?`) — this is precisely what lets a resumed claude (`claude --resume`, same session id, fresh pid) reconnect to its existing subject and pending questions. Keying on PID would orphan the subject on every resume.

Corollary invariant (documented in interaction/channel.go on ChannelTools): (session, scope) must be unique across concurrently-live claude processes. Two live claudes sharing one — e.g. an orchestrated agent on session S scope C plus a manual `cc-runtime wrap -- claude --resume S` in C — ping-pong the subject's pid binding on each ask/notify and share questions/edit-gate state. That is a misconfiguration, not a code defect; no resolver guard can distinguish it from a legitimate resume without a racy PID-liveness probe (PID reuse, restart handoff overlap), so it stays documented rather than coded.
